title: Big Data and Data Science

toc.title: ELT vs. ETL in Big Data

html:
1Definition and Goals

Big Data Definition: Extremely large data sets characterized by high Volume, Velocity, and Variety that cannot be managed with traditional data management tools.

Data Science: Interdiscipline combining statistics, mathematics, programming, and domain knowledge to extract insights from data.

Laney (2001) — Original 3 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety (published by Doug Laney, META Group)

Expanded to 6 Vs:

V Description
Volume Scale of data (terabytes, petabytes, exabytes)
Velocity Speed of data generation and processing
Variety Different types and formats (structured, semi-structured, unstructured)
Veracity Accuracy and trustworthiness of data
Viscosity Resistance to data flow and processing
Virality Rate at which data spreads and is shared
Exam tip

Laney (2001) = 3 Vs original; expanded to 6 Vs total.

3 Goals:

  1. Enable analytics on large, diverse data sets that cannot be handled by traditional tools
  2. Derive competitive insights from new data sources (social media, IoT, logs)
  3. Support data science and machine learning initiatives

2Business Drivers

  • Social media, IoT, machine-generated data exceeding traditional DB capacity
  • Competitive advantage from insights in large unstructured data
  • Reduce costs via commodity hardware (vs. proprietary DW appliances)
  • Enable real-time analytics and event-driven processing
  • Support machine learning and AI applications

3Big Data Architecture

Lambda Architecture

Uses CAP Theorem (from Chapter 6):

  • Speed Layer — provides real-time views; uses Availability + Partition Tolerance
  • Batch Layer — comprehensive, accurate views; uses Consistency + Availability
  • Serving Layer — merges batch and speed views for query

Data Lake

  • Definition: Repository storing raw data in native format until needed
  • Schema on Read — structure applied when data is read (vs. schema on write for relational DW)
  • Data types: structured, semi-structured, unstructured
  • Enables exploratory analytics without pre-defined schema

Data Lake vs. Data Warehouse:

Aspect Data Lake Data Warehouse
Schema Schema on Read Schema on Write
Data State Raw, unprocessed Processed, integrated
Users Data scientists Business analysts
Processing ELT ETL
Structure Flexible Rigid

4Hadoop / MapReduce

Hadoop

  • Open-source distributed computing framework
  • Uses commodity hardware
  • HDFS (Hadoop Distributed File System) — distributed file storage
  • MPP (Massively Parallel Processing) Shared-Nothing architecture — each node independent
  • Designed to fail gracefully; stores multiple copies of data

MapReduce

Three-step computational paradigm:

Step Description
Map Distribute data and task across nodes; process in parallel
Shuffle/Sort Group and sort intermediate results
Reduce Aggregate and combine results from map phase

5ELT vs. ETL in Big Data

ELT (Extract, Load, Transform):

  • Load raw data into data lake first
  • Transform within the target (Hadoop, Spark)
  • Preferred in Big Data environments
  • Target system does the processing work

ETL (Extract, Transform, Load):

  • Transform before loading into target
  • Traditional approach for data warehouses

6Machine Learning

Definition: A subset of AI that gives computers the ability to learn from data without being explicitly programmed.

Three Types of Machine Learning

Type Description Example
Supervised Learning Training data includes labeled inputs and outputs; algorithm learns mapping Spam detection; credit scoring
Unsupervised Learning Training data has no labels; algorithm finds patterns/structure Customer segmentation; anomaly detection
Reinforcement Learning Agent learns by receiving rewards/penalties for actions Game-playing AI; robotics

Common Algorithms

  • Regression — predict continuous values
  • Classification — assign categories
  • Clustering — group similar items (unsupervised)
  • Decision Trees / Random Forests — rule-based classification
  • Neural Networks — deep learning; pattern recognition

PMML (Predictive Model Markup Language)

  • XML-based standard for representing predictive models
  • Enables model portability between tools
  • Used to deploy machine learning models in production

Apache Mahout

  • Open-source machine learning library for Hadoop
  • Scalable algorithms for clustering, classification, collaborative filtering

7Natural Language Processing (NLP)

Definition: Field of AI focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.

Sentiment Analysis:

  • Determines the emotional tone of text (positive, negative, neutral)
  • Applications: social media monitoring, customer feedback analysis
  • Uses NLP techniques

Text Mining:

  • Extracting structured information from unstructured text
  • Applications: document classification, information extraction

8Data Science Activities (7 Key Activities)

Activity 1: Define Big Data Strategy and Business Needs

  • Identify business questions answerable with Big Data
  • Assess data sources and volumes
  • Define technology architecture

Activity 2: Choose Data Sources

  • Identify internal and external data sources
  • Social media, transactional data, machine/sensor data, publicly available datasets
  • Assess data quality and licensing

Activity 3: Acquire and Ingest Data Sources

  • Streaming ingestion (real-time)
  • Batch ingestion (scheduled)
  • Apply Metadata tags during ingestion
  • Data profiling during ingestion identifies domains, relationships, DQ issues

Activity 4: Develop Data Science Models

  • Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
  • Feature engineering
  • Model selection and training
  • Model validation

Activity 5: Deploy and Monitor Models

  • Deploy via PMML or other model serialization formats
  • Monitor model performance and drift
  • Retrain as needed

Activity 6: Publish Insights

  • Visualizations, dashboards, reports
  • Storytelling with data
  • Data journalism

Activity 7: Monitor the Big Data Environment

  • Monitor Hadoop/Spark cluster performance
  • Data ingestion pipelines
  • Model prediction accuracy

9Data Minimization / Privacy

Datensparsamkeit: German concept of "data minimization" — collect only the data necessary for the stated purpose; foundational to EU privacy regulations and GDPR.

Principle: Limit data collection and retention to what is strictly necessary.

Application in Big Data:

  • Big Data tendency is to collect everything ("just in case")
  • Datensparsamkeit pushes back against this with privacy-by-design approach

10NoSQL Databases in Big Data

Definition: "Not Only SQL" databases designed for Big Data workloads.

Type Best For Examples
Key-Value Simple lookups; caching Redis, DynamoDB
Document Semi-structured data (JSON/XML) MongoDB, CouchDB
Column-Family (Wide Column) Analytical queries; sparse data HBase, Cassandra
Graph Relationship networks Neo4j

BASE properties apply (from Chapter 6): Basically Available, Soft State, Eventual Consistency.

11Visualization and Reporting

Data Visualization: Presenting data in graphical/visual format to communicate insights.

Key Tools:

  • R Language — statistical computing and graphics; open-source
  • Python (pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn)
  • Tableau, Power BI — BI visualization tools

R Language: Open-source statistical programming language; widely used in data science and academic research; strong visualization capabilities.

12Services-Based Architecture for Big Data

Three Layers:

Layer Description
Batch Layer Processes and stores large volumes of data; comprehensive but high latency
Speed Layer Processes streaming data in real-time; low latency but approximate
Serving Layer Responds to queries; merges batch and speed layer results

13Governance in Big Data

Key Challenges:

  • Data provenance — where did data come from?
  • Data quality in unstructured data is harder to measure
  • Privacy — PII in unstructured data (social media, logs)
  • Access control — who can access sensitive data in data lake?

Metadata Tagging at Ingestion:

  • Apply Metadata tags when data enters the data lake
  • Tags can identify: data domains, PII, data quality issues, sensitive data
  • Enables governance without schema pre-definition

Data Lake Governance Risk:

  • Without governance, data lake becomes a "data swamp" — unusable due to lack of Metadata

14Practice Q&A

Q1: Who coined the 3 Vs of Big Data and when? A: Doug Laney, META Group, 2001.

Q2: What are the original 3 Vs? A: Volume, Velocity, Variety.

Q3: What are the expanded 6 Vs? A: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, Viscosity, Virality.

Q4: What are the 3 layers of Lambda Architecture? A: Speed Layer (Availability + Partition Tolerance), Batch Layer (Consistency + Availability), Serving Layer (merges results).

Q5: What is the difference between a Data Lake and a Data Warehouse? A: Data Lake = raw data, schema on read, ELT, flexible, for data scientists. Data Warehouse = processed, schema on write, ETL, structured, for business analysts.

Q6: What are the 3 steps of MapReduce? A: Map (distribute and process in parallel), Shuffle/Sort (group intermediate results), Reduce (aggregate results).

Q7: What are the 3 types of machine learning? A: Supervised (labeled data; learns input→output mapping), Unsupervised (no labels; finds patterns), Reinforcement (learns from rewards/penalties).

Q8: What is PMML? A: Predictive Model Markup Language — XML-based standard for representing predictive models; enables model portability between tools.

Q9: What is Apache Mahout? A: Open-source machine learning library for Hadoop; scalable clustering, classification, and collaborative filtering algorithms.

Q10: What is "Datensparsamkeit"? A: German concept of "data minimization" — collect only data necessary for the stated purpose; foundational to privacy-by-design and GDPR.

Q11: What is sentiment analysis? A: NLP technique that determines the emotional tone (positive, negative, neutral) of text; used for social media monitoring and customer feedback analysis.

Q12: What is the difference between ETL and ELT in Big Data? A: ETL transforms before loading (traditional DW approach); ELT loads raw data first then transforms within the target (Big Data/data lake approach using Hadoop/Spark).

Q13: What is MPP Shared-Nothing architecture? A: Massively Parallel Processing where each node is independent (no shared memory or disk); used by Hadoop; enables scaling across commodity hardware.

Q14: What is the "data swamp" risk in data lakes? A: Without governance and Metadata tagging, a data lake becomes unusable — a "data swamp" where data cannot be found or trusted.

Q15: What is the R language? A: Open-source statistical programming language widely used in data science and academic research; strong visualization and statistical analysis capabilities.

15Quick Reference

Concept Key Fact
3 Vs origin Doug Laney, META Group, 2001
3 Vs Volume, Velocity, Variety
6 Vs + Veracity, Viscosity, Virality
Lambda Architecture Speed + Batch + Serving layers
Speed Layer Availability + Partition Tolerance (CAP)
Batch Layer Consistency + Availability (CAP)
Data Lake Raw data; schema on read; ELT
Data Warehouse Processed; schema on write; ETL
MapReduce 3 Steps Map → Shuffle/Sort → Reduce
Hadoop Open-source; MPP Shared-Nothing; HDFS
ELT Load then transform (Big Data)
Supervised Learning Labeled data; learns mapping
Unsupervised Learning No labels; finds patterns
Reinforcement Learning Learns from rewards/penalties
PMML Predictive Model Markup Language; XML; portability
Apache Mahout Open-source ML library for Hadoop
NLP Natural Language Processing
Sentiment Analysis Emotional tone detection from text
Datensparsamkeit Data minimization; German; GDPR foundation
R Language Open-source statistical programming

NoSQL Not Only SQL; Key-Value, Document, Column, Graph
